title: Soap Bubble Nebula, PN G75.5+1.7
caption: The Soap Bubble Nebula (PN G75.5+1.7), imaged by the Mayall 4-meter Telescope
celestial: PN G75.5+1.7, Soap Bubble Nebula · constellation Cygnus

recognition.text: Published in the NSF NOIRLab image archive. No published rating.

story: The planetary nebula nicknamed the Soap Bubble, officially PN G75.5+1.7, is a very round shell of gas in the constellation Cygnus. It lies not far from the Crescent Nebula, NGC 6888.

A planetary nebula is the shell of gas cast off by a dying Sun-like star. Most are irregular in shape, but this shell is spherically symmetric and looks very much like another planetary nebula, Abell 39.

Despite its neat shape, it was found only recently. The Soap Bubble is faint, and it sits within a larger, diffuse nebula, which together kept it hidden from observers. Amateur astronomer Dave Jurasevich discovered it on July 6th, 2008, and Keith Quattrocchi and Mel Helm noted and reported it on July 17th, 2008.

understand.summary: The Mayall 4-meter Telescope's Mosaic camera used two narrowband filters. Hydrogen-alpha is shown in orange and oxygen [O III] in blue.
filters: 499 nm · Optical Olll (NSF Nicholas U. Mayall 4-meter Telescope Mosaic I)
656 nm · Optical Ha (NSF Nicholas U. Mayall 4-meter Telescope Mosaic I)
understand.eye: The nebula is so faint that it went unnoticed until 2008. Narrow filters and a large telescope bring out its shell.

explore: Kitt Peak's Mayall 4-meter telescope captured the nebula on June 19th, 2009, with north pointing left and east down.
alt: A faint, nearly perfectly round shell of gas set within a wider haze of nebulosity and stars.
